lines.en: [Someone has made a ‘Revolutionary Declaration’!]
Even among the countless scenarios of the [Demon Realm], the Revolutionary scenario held great significance.
The only being capable of threatening the [Duke] at the pinnacle of the [Industrial Complex].
The Revolutionary.
That being was the citizens’ hope and legend—and their despair.
That was why, the instant I said those words, countless people all around gasped.
Faces filled with doubt about whether they had heard correctly.
“Why so surprised? Weren’t you looking for the Revolutionary?”
At my shameless tone, their expressions shifted from bewilderment to horror.
At the same time, a message reached only me.
[You are not the ‘Revolutionary’.]
An obvious message.
After all, I was currently an exile outside the scenarios.
There was no way a being who didn’t even have a scenario could become the [Revolutionary], the central figure of the Demon Realm’s main scenario.
Normally, that was how it should have been.
[Your declaration affects the main scenario of the ‘Syswitz Industrial Complex’.]
But as you know, what the <Star Stream> valued most was ‘probability’.
Grrrrrr.
[Re vo lu tion a ry, you say?]
The scythe, wrapped in thick chains, exuded a razor-edged killing intent.
As the [Executioner] took a step closer, I couldn’t help tensing up.
Honestly, even in my current state, I had no way to kill an [Executioner].
Even so, I didn’t back down.
Here, I had to stand my ground.
“Yes. I’m the Revolutionary.”
[Why did you re veal your self?]
“Because someone will die if I don’t step forward.”
Jang Hayoung and the other citizens stared at me, their mouths hanging open.
Watching the approaching [Executioner], I waited anxiously.
······It should be taking effect about now.
[Many citizens admire your courage.]
There we go.
[Your noble courage affects the development of the scenario.]
[You have become a being capable of greatly influencing the scenario.]
[The scenario temporarily assigns you a status.]
[You have become a ‘Self-Proclaimed Revolutionary’.]
[If the existing ‘Revolutionary’ dies, you will inherit that status.]
With this, I too had become a being who could get one foot into a [Scenario].
[You have acquired the hidden scenario—‘Self-Proclaimed Revolutionary’!]
I had never been so glad to hear a scenario acquisition message.
Although it was a time-limited [Hidden Scenario] rather than a [Main Scenario], it should be enough to keep me going for a while.
A hidden scenario of the 73rd Demon Realm.
A secret I would never have known without Yoo Joonghyuk’s countless failures.
“You! Wait! Are you really the Revolutionary?”
“Hey!”
Unable to hold back any longer, people suppressed their fear and sprang up from their tables. But their timing was bad. The [Executioner] had finally begun to move.
Pitch-black smoke poured from the [Executioner]’s mouth and coiled around my body.
[Syswitz’s ‘Executioner’ has placed a death mark on you.]
[You have been designated as the sacrifice for ‘Night’.]
The instant people saw the mark floating around me, they turned deathly pale and shouted.
“Everyone, get out of the way!”
“Waaaaaah!”
Boooooom!

Pieces of a shattered table flew into the air, and the [Executioner]’s scythe descended, slicing through the space ahead. I dodged it by a hair’s breadth. It would have been difficult to avoid that attack if my incarnation body hadn’t been repaired, but things were different now.
[The ‘Exile Penalty’ is partially alleviated.]
The breath I drew in with a sharp hiss carried warmth. A gentle energy settled throughout my body, easing the chill considerably.
With my newly nimble movements, I dodged the [Executioner]’s successive attacks.
As expected, having a scenario made this much of a difference.
Even if it was a hidden scenario rather than a main one, merely entering a story changed how alive my existence felt.
[Re vo lu tion a ry?]
The [Executioner]’s aura changed, as if my movements had surprised it a little.
[The affected space is temporarily sealed.]
[You cannot leave the ‘Tavern’.]
I smiled bitterly.
This was one of the reasons so many powerful beings couldn’t stand against the [Executioners].
As long as you remained inside the [Industrial Complex], there was no way to escape an [Executioner].
And was that all?
“Dodge, you idiot!”
As Jang Hayoung’s voice rang out, an ominous energy erupted from the [Executioner]’s scythe.
「No [Citizen] can stand against an [Executioner].」
[Execution is carried out.]

Its special technique, [Execution], ignored all of its opponent’s defenses and delivered an instant-kill attack. No matter how powerful a [Citizen] might be, they could never block an [Executioner]’s scythe within this scenario.
Shraaaaaak!
The instant the Executioner’s chilling scythe was about to cut through my body.
Eeeeeeeeng!
In my hand, the [Blade of Faith] rang fiercely.
“Sorry, but I’m not a citizen.”
The Gold Dragon’s heart surged, pouring out magic power, and the mighty flow of [White Pure Star Energy] coiled around my fingertips.
“I told you. I’m the ‘Revolutionary’.”
Well, for now, I was merely ‘self-proclaimed’.
Claaaaaang!
The dazzling White Pure magic collided with the Executioner’s scythe, spraying tremendous sparks. Amid the brilliant crackling, system messages sounded.
[You are not a main scenario participant.]
[You are not a ‘Citizen’.]
[You are an ‘Exile’.]
[You are not affected by this scenario’s ‘Execution’ effect.]
Just as expected. I knew it.
[The instant-kill effect of ‘Execution’ is neutralized.]
Krrrrrrrk!
As I deflected the [Executioner]’s scythe, the incarnations around me cried out in shock.
“H-he withstood an Executioner’s blow!”
“Is he really the Revolutionary?”
Those who didn’t know my identity watched what was happening with eyes full of disbelief.
[Your contribution to the scenario increases.]
The [Executioner] seemed to have thoroughly misunderstood me as well; a terrifying aura blazed from its entire body.
[In so lent······!]
I spoke, as if to provoke it.
“Don’t get cocky. I know you’re only strong at night.”
[What?]
“When this night ends, you will definitely die.”
I spoke, slowly turning my wrist with [Unbreakable Faith] in hand.
“Because I will kill you. Without fail.”
Kaboom!
The scythe split into dozens of shadows (分影) that rushed toward me. Just because [Execution] didn’t work didn’t mean the [Executioner] was weak.
It would simply take longer to dispose of me.
So it was too early to say the situation had improved.
“I can’t protect everyone, so get outside!”
Everyone except me was unaffected by the ‘mark’, so they could escape freely. Among the people scrambling out of the tavern, I saw Jang Hayoung look back at me.
I glanced briefly at Hayoung, then quietly activated [Bookmark].
“I select Bookmark No. 4, ‘Lycaon Isparang’.”
[The exclusive skill, ‘Way of the Wind Lv.10(+1)’, is activated!]
Using [Kyrgios]’s power in Bookmark No. 5 would make this opponent easier to handle, but winning wasn’t the point of this fight.
No, I couldn’t win.
[Your attacks have no effect on the target.]
[No one can kill an ‘Executioner’ until ‘Night’ ends.]
My swinging blade cut through its collar, but all I got in return were those messages.
Its [Execution] didn’t work on me, but none of my attacks could hurt it during the industrial complex’s night, either.
I needed to change tactics.
Whooooooosh!
The area around the tavern was devastated as the wind’s power began to rage. The dozens of scythe shadows swooping down through the air slowed as they became entangled in the wind’s movements.
My movements, meanwhile, grew even more agile. The balance of speed was breaking down. Its movements were always a beat slower than mine, and mine were always a step ahead of its.
This was the essence of [Way of the Wind] pushed to its limit.
The power to control all acceleration (加速) within the surrounding space.
“Can you even see me when you’re that sluggish?”
[G r a a a a a.]
The enraged [Executioner] began slashing wildly through the air with its scythe.
Normally, there was no way I would let attacks like that hit me.
But perhaps that damned goddess of fortune from <Olympus> had smiled on it, because one randomly swung scythe slipped into my blind spot.
“Oops.”
Just as the unexpected blow was about to strike my side, my right arm suddenly twisted into a strange position and blocked it.
[The Sword Master’s talent dwelling in your right arm shines!]
Claaaaang!
I was just as surprised.
Who would have thought a Story fragment could exert its power like this?
[Using an incomplete Story destabilizes your incarnation body’s state.]
[Your Stories may be endangered if you continue excessive combat.]
I bit down hard on my lip.
The chill, slowly creeping back in.
After going to the trouble of acquiring a [Hidden Scenario], I couldn’t use excessive power just to deal with one [Executioner].
I couldn’t keep fighting it head-on.
I had to dodge as much as possible and buy time.
Until this damned [Night] ended.
[You wi ll d ie.]
Without answering, I activated [Way of the Wind] at full power.
Whoooooosh!
It would have been nice if Yoo Joonghyuk were here.
With his help as a transcendent, enduring this long night would have been easier.
But no one was here.
Not the ‘Judge of Evil’, Jung Heewon.
Not the ‘Steel Sword Emperor’, Lee Hyunsung.
Not the ‘Maritime Admiral’, Lee Jihye.
Not even my lovely little ones, Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung.
Han Sooyoung······ Well, she wouldn’t have helped even if she were here.
Cl-cl-cl-clang!
Here, I was alone.
All I could trust was the information I had.
The stories I had built up.
And myself.
Amid the frightened people’s screams, the [Executioner]’s attacks began to slow little by little. I spoke to it mockingly.
“What’s this? Tired?”
I knew there was no way a being judged invincible would get tired.
It was probably getting annoyed instead.
I had actually said that to conceal my own condition.
[Bookmark’s duration is nearly over.]
Thirty minutes was the most I could hold out with [Way of the Wind].
To begin with, [Bookmark] wasn’t a skill that could last very long.
But the [Executioner] was smiling.
Whooooooosh!
Ten or so [Executioners], appearing in midair with a spine-chilling sound.
The most horrifying thing about this night was that there wasn’t just one [Executioner].
All the [Executioners] of the [Syswitz Industrial Complex] had gathered inside the cramped tavern and were glaring at me.
[Your mis take.]
It had deliberately pretended to stall while gathering its companions. To make absolutely certain it finished me off this night.
Whoooosh.
Watching the [Executioners] surround me, radiating killing intent, I adjusted my stance.
I couldn’t dodge this.
Even with [Way of the Wind], escaping them would be impossible.
But.
“No. You’re the one who made a mistake.”
Having stalled for a full thirty minutes, I had more than achieved my goal.
Watching the procession of approaching scythes, I spread my arms.
Ka-ka-ka-ka-boom!

The countless scythes flew toward me, shattering the very air, and pierced my torso. Some incarnations squeezed their eyes shut and let out anguished groans. But before long, their cries turned to astonishment.
Eeeeeeeeng.
The scythes that should surely have pierced and torn me apart.
Those scythes had stopped in midair.
[Wh at?]
The bewildered [Executioners] stared blankly at their weapons suspended in the air.
I recalled a passage from ‘Ways of Survival’.
「There are two ways to endure the industrial complex’s ‘Night’.」
「One is to keep fleeing the ‘Executioners’ until ‘Night’ ends.」
「And the other is······.」
“Did you forget? The [Revolutionary] and [Executioners] aren’t the only ones in this scenario.”
Then, a message sounding in my ears.
[Someone is using their vitality to protect you.]
「The second way to survive ‘Night’ is to receive help from the ‘Guardian’.」
Just as expected. I knew this would bring the hidden ‘Guardian’ out.
Aileen had said
that even the members of the Citizens’ Council didn’t know who the [Revolutionary] was.
That meant the other incarnations didn’t know who the [Revolutionary] was, either.
In other words, even if they wanted to offer protection, they couldn’t because they didn’t know whom to protect.
But what if, in that situation, the [Revolutionary] appeared and revealed themselves?
[Protection was successful, and the death mark has been removed!]
Only one mark each night allowed the [Executioners] to run rampant.
With the mark removed, tonight’s killing was over.
The [Executioner] spoke in a murderous voice.
[······You were lu cky.]
“You’d better be careful. Next time we meet, it’ll be ‘Day’.”
Seemingly resentful, the [Executioners] ground their teeth and dispersed into the air one by one.
The eerie piping faded, and the darkness ebbed away like a receding tide.

Outside the tavern, I could see incarnations looking my way with excited eyes. Even the aloof Jang Hayoung was staring at me in shock. I wondered whether I should say something, then simply gave an awkward wave.
“A-a new Revolutionary! A new Revolutionary has appeared!”
Amid the citizens’ cheers, the short night was finally retreating.
Looking at those citizens, I thought.
One of them would be the ‘Guardian’.
I absolutely had to carry out the coming scenarios together with the ‘Guardian’.
When I looked up, the dark night sky was still there.
Occasionally, I could make out a few things resembling stars, but they were so faint that I could barely see them.
Uriel, or the Great Sage, Heaven’s Equal······.
It would have been nice if they were watching, but unfortunately, no messages came.
Still, I would have to be satisfied with this much for today.
[No one died tonight.]
Outside Duke Syswitz’s office.
The demon earl Silocke had been pacing anxiously outside it for dozens of minutes already. It was because of Earl ‘Han’, who guarded the office like a gatekeeper.
‘Han’.
No one knew his real name.
He was called that simply because everyone called him ‘Han’.

He held the same rank as Silocke, ‘earl’, but his background was quite different. He had connections to none other than ‘Asmodeus’, the Demon King of the 32nd Demon Realm. Duke Syswitz probably kept him close because he was well aware of that.
Feeling inwardly intimidated, Silocke spoke.
“I have something important to tell the duke.”
“Tell me. I’ll pass it on.”
“That won’t do.”
“The duke is currently in an emergency meeting with the [Gilobat] delegation.”
“When will he be finished?”
“I don’t know that, either.”
Silocke clicked his tongue inwardly.
If he told this bastard, Han would surely take all the credit.
So Silocke answered like this.
“Never mind. It isn’t urgent, so I’ll wait.”
Han’s eyebrow twitched at those words.
Silocke enjoyed seeing that expression on Han’s face.
‘You son of a bitch. Keep wondering.’
In fact, what Silocke had to report was simple.
—A ‘demon noble’ believed to be a marquis from [Gilobat] had appeared in the citizens’ district.
Of course, put that way, it didn’t sound like much, but the more he thought about it, the more strange things he found about the incident.
After thinking for a moment, Silocke cast a casual glance toward the duke’s office and asked.
“Is the marquis from [Gilobat] in there as well, by any chance?”
“He is.”
“He must have come straight here without stopping anywhere else.”
“Given the matter at hand.”
At that businesslike reply, Silocke inwardly rejoiced.
‘As I thought. My guess was right.’
He couldn’t be certain, but the [Gilobat] delegation was unlikely to include two marquises. Someone of a marquis’s rank would at least serve as the head of a delegation.
In other words, the fellow playing the demon noble in the citizens’ streets was probably not a marquis from [Gilobat].
That alone gave his report value as a ‘report’.
Even if it wasn’t a major case, it would help his record a little.
Whatever he thought upon seeing Silocke hesitate, Han asked.
“Since you keep hanging around, you must be curious about who the next ‘Demon King’ will be, too.”
“Ah, well. Yes.”
It was a misunderstanding, of course, but since he had already been misunderstood, he thought it wouldn’t hurt to ask about it.
“So the [Gilobat Delegation] came because of the rumors that a Demon King will appear?”
“I can’t tell you the details, but something like that.”
“A Demon King, after all this time. It’s a little absurd······ Don’t you think?”
A rumor whose origin wasn’t even clearly known.
And that single rumor had the entire ‘73rd Demon Realm’ in such an uproar.
Silocke privately found the situation ridiculous.
Syswitz.
Gilobat.
Melledon.
Bercan.

For the past several hundred years, these four dukes had maintained a proper balance in the 73rd Demon Realm. Yet a single rumor was shaking a peace that had lasted hundreds of years. Somehow, it didn’t seem real.
But Han’s expression showed that he didn’t agree with Silocke.
“Signs of a ‘Demon King’ are already appearing.”
“What? How do you know?”
“I hear <Vedas> has joined hands with the [Melledon Industrial Complex].”
“<Vedas>?”
It was a name Silocke knew well, too.
No, it would have been strange not to know it.
It was one of the names you absolutely had to know to live safely in the <Star Stream>.
That was why Silocke couldn’t help being shocked.
“······Are you saying a <Nebula> has taken action itself?”
“To be precise, they say one of <Vedas>’s Narrative-grade constellations has made contact with [Melledon].”
Constellations and Demon Kings were among the bitterest enemies in the entire <Star Stream>.
Yet the constellations had interfered in the affairs of the ‘73rd Demon Realm’, despite the opposition of the Demon Kings.
It didn’t seem to be on a large scale yet, but if a <Nebula> really had stepped in, this was no simple matter.
“The nebulas are taking an interest. Is a ‘Demon King’ really going to appear······?”
Silocke muttered those words, his gaze somewhat dazed.
But a Demon King.
Even Silocke, who had spent so long in the Demon Realm, couldn’t quite grasp it.
Still, there was at least one thing he could understand.
“······So that’s why the duke has been so busy.”
“He is currently the closest to becoming a ‘Demon King’.”
It was clear that one of the demon nobles would rise to the position of ‘Demon King’.
Looking at the other 72 Demon Kings, cases in which a being other than a demon had ascended to the throne were exceedingly rare······.
It was then that a message appeared, accompanied by a faint warning tone that rang throughout the [Factory].
[A new main scenario has opened!]
[The 24th ‘Revolutionary Game’ has begun.]
Silocke was startled by the sudden message, but seeing Han’s surprised expression, he forced himself to act calm. Han asked first.
“What is this message?”
“Ah, you haven’t been here long, so you wouldn’t know. This happens from time to time here. It’s this place’s main scenario. The Revolutionary Game.”
“The Revolutionary Game?”
“He must have been hiding and gotten caught by an [Executioner]. An incredibly unlucky bastard.”
The start of the ‘Revolutionary Game’ meant that the hidden ‘Revolutionary’ had appeared.
But there was no way a Revolutionary had truly come forward in this industrial complex.
Everyone in the industrial complex remembered all too clearly what had happened to the last Revolutionary who appeared, thirty years ago.
Silocke added with a smile.
“It’s nothing, so don’t worry. Wait a little, and the [Executioners] will bring back his severed head on their own. We’ll have something entertaining to watch for the first time in a while.”
But no matter how long they waited, no message announcing the game’s end came.
Just as he began to think something was strange, a lesser noble appeared.
Silocke immediately recognized him.
Because he was one of the hidden [Executioners].
As the man came running breathlessly toward the office, Silocke spoke first.
“What’s happened?”
“Someone has made a ‘Revolutionary Declaration’!”
Though he knew it was a foolish question, Silocke couldn’t help asking.
“What? Who?”
“A new Revolutionary!”
“I’m asking what the bastard’s name is.”
The lesser noble stammered out a name. It was a name Silocke didn’t know. Unexpectedly, however, Han, who had looked bored all day, brightened and asked.
“Wait. What did you just say?”
“Yes, definitely someone called ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’······.”
“He said he was Yoo Joonghyuk?”
Silocke hurriedly asked.
“Do you know him?”
“Of course I do.”
The face of ‘Han’ was glowing. Yet rather than a smile, there was something twisted about his expression. A face that sent a chill through even Silocke, a demon. ‘Han’ asked.
“Where did he appear?”
After Night retreated, Aileen summoned me again.
To be precise, I was practically dragged there.
Because my declaration had turned the citizens’ streets completely upside down.
—A new Revolutionary has appeared!

Shouts like that rang throughout the streets. If Aileen hadn’t suddenly appeared and hauled me into the council office, I would still have been caught in the throng of citizens. While Aileen huffed, unable to control her emotions, I calmly checked the [Hidden Scenario] information.
<Hidden Scenario — Fake Revolutionary>
Category: Hidden
Difficulty: SS

Clear Conditions: By impersonating the Revolutionary, you have become a ‘Self-Proclaimed Revolutionary’. Kill the real Revolutionary within the allotted time and inherit their position. Otherwise, you will meet a horrific end.
Time Limit: 30 days
Reward: 150,000 coins, entry into a new main scenario.
Failure: Death
I had a rough idea of how to enter the main scenario now.
In any case, I had to find the real ‘Revolutionary’······.
I looked at Aileen and spoke.
“All right. Start asking questions.”
“······Are you insane?”
Aileen looked incredulous.
“Do you know what you’ve done?”
“A revolution.”
“A revolution? What revolution? You’re a fake!”
“What if I’m real?”
“There’s no way······ Could you possibly······?”
The way she asked, just in case, was cute.
When I gave a light shrug, despair spread across Aileen’s face.
“Of course you couldn’t be! What on earth were you thinking, doing that? Now we’re all finished!”
I answered shamelessly.
“This is the development you wanted, too. A revolution, and killing the duke.”
“Certainly not like this! This is a fraud!”
“What makes a revolution real or fake? If it succeeds, it’s real.”
“A revolution isn’t some word game!”
“I agree with your cause. I didn’t make that Revolutionary Declaration lightly, either. I’m saying I agree that this [Industrial Complex] needs to be liberated.”
“The very fact that you can say it so easily proves how shallow your commitment is.”
Deep anger filled Aileen’s voice.
“Do you think a ‘revolution’ will happen just because you step forward on your own?”
“I’ve watched revolutions in this [Industrial Complex] for a long time. How many have failed, how much blood has been spilled. And······.”
“Don’t treat past failures like scripture. Nothing will change if you do nothing.”
“It’s an impossible scenario to begin with!”
I understood Aileen’s feelings well.
In fact, the ‘Revolutionary Scenario’ had already become a scenario in name only within the [Industrial Complex].
The only protocol for rebellion permitted by the scenario.
Even so, the [Citizens] of the [Industrial Complex] had given up on this game long ago.
Because they had no chance of winning.
And so the scenario had lost its worth as a scenario.
Aileen continued shouting.

“That’s why I’ve been relying on ‘exiles’. Because there’s absolutely no way to kill the duke through the existing scenario! Never mind the duke—we don’t even have a way to defeat those damned [Executioners]!”
“Scenarios are made to be cleared. Look closely enough, and there’s a way to clear them.”
“People will die. Because of you.”
“I won’t let that happen.”
“Then you’ll be the first to die.”
“I won’t die. I didn’t die earlier, did I?”
“That was······!”
Biting down hard on her lip, Aileen spoke.
“That was just luck. Do you think that ‘Guardian’ will protect you again?”
“Hmm. I think they will.”

“You may not know this, but protection by a ‘Guardian’ consumes ‘vitality’. Their points decrease with every use, and eventually they die. Once is one thing, but no one will protect you twice or three times!”
“Whatever you’re doing, that first time matters.”
“Aileen, you know more about this place than I do, but you don’t seem to know much about people.”
Aileen had been about to say something, but for the first time, she pressed her lips shut.
Despite what she was saying, Aileen was probably feeling something, too.
The hidden [Guardian] had come forward.
And they had protected me, someone claiming to be the [Revolutionary].
It had probably been a very long time since Aileen had seen something like that.
A very, very long time.
After moving her lips for a long while, Aileen muttered quietly.
“Do you really think it’s possible?”
“It is. You’ve seen enough of what I can do, haven’t you?”
It would be possible.
Even if it wasn’t, I would make it possible.
Aileen’s reply was almost a sigh.
“But you aren’t the ‘Revolutionary’.”
“That’s why I need your help.”
At my words, Aileen’s expression wavered.
“Let’s make a revolution without a ‘Revolutionary’.”
Eventually, as if she had made up her mind about something, Aileen spoke.
“······We need to gather the positions. This is a game you can’t win alone.”
“I suppose so.”
“A [Guardian] is only the bare minimum needed to survive. We also need a [Fighter] to face the [Executioners], and a [Spy] to find the hidden [Executioners].”
“We can gather them one at a time. Those ‘positions’ probably aren’t as far away as you think.”
I wasn’t anxious.
Now that the ‘Revolutionary Declaration’ had rung out, the beings holding each position would have begun to realize where they stood, one by one.
They were probably weighing for themselves whose side to take in this damned game.
“And I think we’ve already gathered one.”
No sooner had I spoken than the council office door creaked open. Jang Hayoung was peeking through it at us.
“Um, Aileen······.”
“What?”
“Someone’s insisting we let them in······.”
“I told you I’m busy! Send them away.”
“Well, that’s a little······.”
“Why?”
“······A human’s here claiming to be the [Guardian].”
Startled, Aileen sprang to her feet.
Then a sturdily built middle-aged man appeared behind Jang Hayoung.
“You······ Are you really the ‘Revolutionary’?”
Surprisingly, it was a face I already knew.

The person who opened the door and appeared was a thin-looking middle-aged man. Hair streaked with scattered gray strands, and a grime-stained apron. A faint scar on his clean-shaven cheek was the only sign of ‘strength’ to be found in his face.
No matter how I looked at him, he didn’t seem like someone who could ‘protect’ anyone. Aileen stared at him in disbelief, then dropped back into her seat and spoke.
“You’re the [Guardian]?”
“For now, yes.”
“······Really?”
“I was worried you’d react like this.”
At the middle-aged man’s words, Aileen looked at me. I gave her a gentle smile.
“I told you. They’d be nearby.”
“But I didn’t think they’d be this close······.”
The [Guardian] was the tavern owner who had made me food to go with my drinks earlier.
Of course, I had suspected he was the Guardian from the beginning.
Because he looked very much like the [Guardian] described in ‘Ways of Survival’.
I had also already known he would save me.
If I hadn’t, I wouldn’t have made the ‘Revolutionary Declaration’ in the first place.
Aileen asked.
“Why have you done nothing until now? If you really were the [Guardian], you had plenty of opportunities to save people.”
“Because I had to conserve my points. As you know, a Guardian can save someone once a day, only five times in total.”
“That’s true, but as long as you didn’t use all five······.”
“If I had saved someone else.”
The tavern owner glanced at me and continued.
“That ‘Revolutionary’ would have died.”
“You speak as if you knew a Revolutionary would appear.”
“I was always waiting. Not everyone had given up like you, Aileen.”
“······Are you finished?”
As the mood threatened to grow heated, Jang Hayoung quickly intervened.
“Now, now, Aileen. Boss. Stop fighting and think about what comes next. The [Guardian] coming forward on his own is good for us, isn’t it?”

I inwardly admired that skillful change of subject. Jang Hayoung was one of the most perceptive characters in ‘Ways of Survival’. Here, pent-up urges were running wild, earning Hayoung the nickname ‘Foulmouth’, but originally, Jang Hayoung was an outstanding mediator who understood people’s hearts better than anyone.
As the tavern owner cleared his throat, Jang Hayoung patted his shoulder and spoke.
“Anyway, you surprised me, too, boss. I thought cooking was all you were good at. Honestly, you could’ve given us a hint, couldn’t you?”
“A good cook has plenty of secrets. Speaking of which, Revolutionary, how was my cooking earlier?”
“Unfortunately, I didn’t get to try it. Someone ate it all.”
As Jang Hayoung glared at me through narrowed eyes, the tavern owner chuckled. It was Aileen who threw cold water on the mood again, just as it finally began to improve.

The Exile Penalty.
There was no one in this Demon Realm who didn't know what it was.
That was why people chose instead to spin the roulette of death once every three days. But since the ‘Revolutionary’ had appeared, the interval between spins had shortened from three days to one.
“D-do we have to endure a [Night] like this every day now?”
“What are you going to do now! What are you going to do about this!”
Voices gripped by fear.
Aileen and the other council members tried to restrain them, but the crowd only grew more agitated. Turning my head, I found Aurelius watching me with a nasty smile.
“Do you understand what's happening now?”
A [Revolutionary] without the citizens' support was bound to lose.
I smiled bitterly.
“You're on the [Duke's] side.”
“That isn't important. What matters is your choice.”
“So what do you want?”
“Surrender to the duke. Then everyone but you can live. The revolution will fail anyway if things continue like this.”
“You're telling me to sacrifice myself?”
“That's not what I mean. I'll find a way for you to survive too.”
“How?”
“If you really are Yoo Joonghyuk, the one I serve will protect you.”
“The duke will try to kill me, though?”
“Duke Syswitz doesn't even begin to compare to the one I serve.”
Someone Duke Syswitz couldn't even begin to compare to.
It was an offer that piqued my curiosity.
If I hadn't been Yoo Joonghyuk, I might have considered it for a moment.
“Obviously, I refuse.”
“I see. You'll regret that.”
The next moment, Aurelius had vanished from my side.
Then someone in the crowd shouted.
“Let's hand him over to the [Duke]!”
“The [Duke] said he'd end the ‘scenario’ if we brought him that man!”
“[Night] won't come anymore!”
Voices rising and spreading like wildfire, as if they had arranged it beforehand.
Very interesting.
In fact, I had seen a similar scene once before.
I thought it had probably been during the labor-management negotiations at ‘Mino Soft’.
“When the next [Night] comes, we're all finished! We have to catch the Revolutionary before then!”
The sheer force of that incitement was swaying the crowd. Their frightened faces turned hostile, and that hostility became resistance to me.
“S-someone catch him······!”
I watched them for a moment, then stepped forward to meet the crowd.
When I walked out without fear, it was the crowd that became flustered.
People backed away to avoid touching me, parting around me like the waters before Moses.
“Are the [Executioners] that frightening?”

I took another step and drew [Unbreakable Faith]. [Blade of Faith] vibrated violently and burst into brilliant white light. My voice, infused with magic power, washed over the crowd like cold water. Startled by the wave of magic, some fell on their backsides, while others stumbled backward in alarm. I spoke to them in a quiet voice.
“You all seem to have forgotten, but it isn't [Night] right now.”

I raised my sword into the air. The waves of magic from [White Pure Star Energy], pouring from the gold dragon's heart, began staining the black sky with White Pure light. Frightened by my sudden action, the people shouted.
“He's going to kill someone!”
“Aaaaaaagh! The Revolutionary is killing citizens!”
The startled people screamed, and I heard Aileen shouting. But I ignored all those sounds and ran through the center of the crowd.
Then, without hesitation, I swung my blade at one of them.
“First, one.”
Thwack!
It was one of the men who had been stirring up the crowd moments earlier. With his heart mercilessly pierced, he stared at me with wide eyes, unable even to scream, and died.
[The exclusive skill, ‘Fourth Wall’, is activated!]
The sensation of killing settling into my fingertips.
It had been a while since I had moved with the clear intention of killing someone.
Probably because the restraint I'd practiced for so long to maintain ‘King of No Killing’ had become a habit.
But today, I didn't hesitate in the slightest.
As if I really had become Yoo Joonghyuk.
“And two.”
Moving to ensure a kill, the blade drank blood and gave off a sinister aura.
Then the second man's head flew off.
Pshhhhh!
Blood sprayed fiercely, soaking the front of my clothes, and I saw the people's terrified faces.
I moved my sword again, driving it into the last man's back.
“Finally, three.”
After killing three people in an instant, I looked around.
Everyone in the citizens' district, engulfed in screams, cries, and grief, was looking at me.
Not just the citizens.
Aileen, Jang Hayoung, and Mark too.
Their faces showed panic; they couldn't understand what I had done.
The Revolutionary had killed ordinary [citizens].
Whatever I said, no explanation could make that acceptable.
But I had never needed to explain it in the first place.
[A change has occurred in the ‘Revolutionary Scenario’!]
At the sudden message, everyone looked up into the air at once.
Then, messages appearing in succession.
[An ‘Executioner’ has been killed by someone.]
[An ‘Executioner’ has been killed by someone.]
[An ‘Executioner’ has been killed by someone.]
[Current number of remaining Executioners: 7]
As people read the message, the looks on their faces began to change.
Three people had died in total.
And three Executioners had died too.
The people who had stared at me with trembling eyes were now screaming and backing away from the corpses.
As if they were looking at something horrific.
“A-aaaaaagh!”
“E-Executioners? They were hiding here?”
“Aaron was an Executioner! My God!”
[Executioners] had been hiding among the [citizens].
Amid that overwhelming sense of betrayal, the crowd was slowly waking up.
The Executioners had died.
The Executioners they had believed invincible had died like ordinary people.
A story they had never experienced before.
Confronted with that story, the people were being roused in an unexpected way.
The first person to get up drew a blade from inside their clothes.
Their eyes now blazed with unprecedented anger.
“Y-you sons of bitches! Good riddance, you sons of bitches!”

The people who had been threatening me moments before began trampling and hacking at the dead [Executioners'] corpses. The crowd seethed with several times its earlier fury. They were all people who had lost something to the [Executioners]. It was a wretched revenge, but it was the best they could do.
I walked unhurriedly through that crowd.
Then I caught the man trying to slip away by the scruff of his neck.
“Gaaack!”
“You're still as skilled at stirring people up as ever.”
The man who had been trying to flee struggled in my grip.
“Have you been well, Department Manager Han Myungoh?”
